meaning: quarrelsome.
to ride hard.

meaning: dainty, well-formed, well-fitting.

meaning: a thick-headed, dull, heavy person.
the sound of a great bell.

quote: Nor when any of them are wounded, pot-shot, jug-bitten, or cup-shaken, so that they have lost all reasonable faculties of the mind.

meaning: from jimp or jimply, suitably, opportunely.
quote: My meeting so jumply with them, makes me abashed with the strangeness of it.

meaning: crooked; from the Gaelic cam.

quote: He ended and the kebars shook.

meaning: a fat round lump, a keg (of butter).

quote: When the tod (fox) is in the wood, he cares na how many keek at his tail.

meaning: deserving of a kiss, inspiring affection.
quote: Thy most kiss-worthy face, / Anger invests with such lovely grace, / That Anger's self I needs must kiss again.

quote: If you love me, kythe it.

meaning: difficult, perilous, ticklish.
quote: It's kittle to waken sleeping dogs.

meaning: obsequious, slavish in homage.

a button or a bud; a word in common use before the English people began to import their fashions as well as their speech from the continent; and one form of which still survives as knob, the knob or button of a door.

meaning: sometimes written nirl, to shrink up with the cold.
quote: The corn has been nirled with the drowth.

meaning: a rough, ignorant, ill-tempered fellow, a churl, from the French cuistre.
a grimace.
a person who lived a long while ago, (Northumbrian and Scottish).
having lost or been dismissed by a mistress.

quote: Whistle o'er the lave o't.

meaning: cessation or soothing.
empty.
quote: This word is sufficiently common in every part of Devonshire; a leer stomach, an empty stomach.

meaning: to approve, to be highly in favour of anything.
quote: Leeze me on the spinning-wheel.

meaning: a lover; originally applied to both sexes, but in progress of time, and in the improvement, or may be corruption of the language, applied solely to the female; and by a still later corruption, to signify a mistress, as distinguished from a wife.

meaning: to shine; a light.
quote: With lily-white cheek and leming eye, / She look'd and laughed to him.

meaning: a lie, a falsehood.
quote: For we lived on the lesynges.

meaning: to please.
quote: And saide, lordes! harkeneth if you lest.

quote: Unhand me, gentlemen! / By heaven! I'll make a ghost of him that lets me!

meaning: the lightning.
quote: And when the flashing leven leaps to light / Upon two stubborn oaks.

meaning: a thunderbolt.
quote: His burning levin-brand in hand he took.

meaning: an indecent, lewd, obscene person.
quote: Against such lewdsters and their lechery, / Those that betray them do no treachery.

meaning: dear.
quote: Oft have I heard my lief Corydon report on a love day.

meaning: the sky, the air, the atmosphere.
quote: When the lift grew dark, and the wind blew hard.

meaning: from the German liegen, to lie down. This ancient word is still in common use in Cumberland and Northumberland, and also in the Border Counties of Scotland.
quote: I have ligged for a fortnight in London, weak almost to death, and neglected by every one.
quote_source: G. P. R. James: Gowrie, or the King's Plot

meaning: a linnet.
quote: But oh! sir, there are no linties in the woods and no braes like Yarrow.

meaning: wise of talk or lip, as distinguished from wise in brain or thought.
to rely or depend upon, to take a liking to.
quote: Never lippen too much to a new friend or an old enemy.

meaning: pleasure, akin to bliss, and possibly the original form of that word.
quote: Lisse without an ende.

meaning: movable property.
the forget-me-not.
wicked, lazy, wickedly idle.
quote: If he were as long as he is lither, he might thatch a house without a ladder.

a pilot.

the grave.
tedious.
the hollow of the hand. From the Gaelic lamh, pronounced laf, the hand.

meaning: a teacher.
a dissolute person.

meaning: flattery, lying.
quote: In lecherie and losengeries / Ye liven and in sleuthe.

meaning: to make a curtsey, or an obeisance, to bow down.
quote: They louted to that ladye.

meaning: amiable.
quote: Oh, lovesome ladie bright! / How have ye fared since that ye were there?

quote: The sacred lowe o' weel placed love, / Luxuriantly indulge it.

meaning: still, calm.
quote: Oh, your chamber is very dark, fair maid, / And the night is wondrous lown.
quote_source: Ballad of Sir Roland, in Motherwell's Collection

heavy, cumbrous, difficult, to lug or drag along.
a lazy lubber.

meaning: shiny.
from the Gaelic liath, grey; a grey horse.

meaning: to stammer, to stutter.

to gape about stupidly; to 'moon.'

domestic servants, menials.

to conceal.
a dunghill.
to cover with a veil.

drops of perspiration.

stark or utterly naked, naked as a new-born babe.

the toll or tax taken by a miller for grinding corn.

meaning: moist.

dirt, filth, whence the adjective, nasty.

hemp; a metaphorical expression for a rope.

wickedness.

lumpy, knotty; whence, metaphorically, cross-grained, and ill-tempered.

diligent.

all sorts of odds and ends, occasional.

a sale by auction.

sanguineness.

wet, spongy, morassy, boggy; applied to land.
a grandchild.
a cowslip.

peas. Formerly peas was employed in the singular, and the word pea, as now used, was unknown.

the officer whose duty it was to impound strayed animals.
a pound for strayed animals.

a stream.
to glean in an orchard.
a piece of money.
moneyless.

full of decorations and adornments, lively, frolicsome.

meaning: leaning to, addicted to, having a 'proclivity' for.

to poke, push, and peer about; to maraud, for the purpose of plunder; whence the modern slang prog, originally meaning food taken from the people by an invading army; but now food in general, as in the phrase, 'my prog and my grog,' i.e., my food and my drink.

meaning: brave, courageous; whence prowess, bravery, strength.

tough and indigestible.
a stone quarry.
to block up.
to shake, to quiver.

meaning: pleasure.
to spin round, to coil, to twirl.
joyful, in good spirits.
quote: He was now in quert, / And all hale of wille and herte.

a play upon words; a facetious subtlety of argument, without logical force.
quote: Ply her with love-letters and billets, / And bait them well with quirks and quillets.

meaning: a northern word, signifying a piece of enclosed land on a common.
pieces of supple underwood, twisted between upright stakes to form a fence.

meaning: roughness, coarseness, rashness.

a public meeting, or fair; whence, perhaps, the word ranter, a priest or layman who preached to the crowd on such occasions.

quote: Oh dear, cousin mine, dear John, she said, / What aileth you so rathe for to arise?

meaning: to advise, to counsel.

meaning: a healthy complexion; the redness of one red with the blood of life; whence ruddy.

to comfort.
hoarse, as with bronchitis or sore throat.

meaning: to praise; to drink a health.
